# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

**Iteration 3 / 5, candidate `cand_0003`, parent `cand_0002` (val 1.000).**

## Headline

**I shipped NO capability edit, deliberately.** Two independent findings force that, and both
are verified from this iteration's own data rather than inherited from a predecessor:

1. **There is no failing cluster to fix.** All 40 val tasks score `reward = 1.0`, with
   `soft_no_recalc = hard_no_recalc = soft_restriction = hard_restriction = 1.0` and
   `test_case_results = test_case_results_no_recalc = [1]`. There is no reward-0 task, no
   partial-credit task, and no multi-test-case task with a failing case. The framework's own
   focus line agrees: *"No actionable failures in focus."* By the **REAL** test — *"it targets a
   cluster that is FAILING in THIS iteration's `./trajectories/`"* — **zero** candidate edits
   qualify. Keeping one anyway would be the speculative edit the brief forbids.
2. **No candidate can be ACCEPTED this iteration, as a matter of arithmetic.** The gate is
   `ACCEPT iff mean_i(cand_i − parent_i) > 0.2·SE` (verbatim from the gate's own reason strings
   in `reused_seed_run/run_suite/rejected.jsonl`). The parent is stored at `reward = 1.0` on
   **every** one of the 40 tasks, per-task reward is capped at 1.0, and the parent is **not
   re-measured** (`state.json`: `metric_calls = 80`, `iterations = 2`, `n_val = 40` → 40 calls
   per iteration, i.e. the candidate only; `best_val = 1.0`). Therefore `cand_i − parent_i ≤ 0`
   for every task, so `Δ̄ ≤ 0 ≤ 0.2·SE` and the bar can never be cleared. This holds for
   iterations 4 and 5 too, unchanged.

So the honest, maximum-value output of this iteration is an accurate hand-back, in the spirit of
the brief's own rule that *"handing back an accurate 'here is the evidence' is a SUCCESSFUL
iteration"*. The evidence, the one real latent defect I found, and a correction to a
previously-recorded "refutation" are below.

## Ranked issue list (clusters, biggest first)

No cluster is a *failure* cluster. Ranked by what they would be worth **if** val had headroom:

| # | Cluster | Tasks | Tag | Status | Recoverable score on val |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Step-3 verify snippet crashes on a single-cell `answer_position`** — `task_template.md:97` hands the agent `cells = [c.coordinate for row in graded[RNG] for c in row]`; openpyxl returns a bare `Cell` (not a tuple of row tuples) when `RNG` names one cell, so this raises `TypeError: 'Cell' object is not iterable` | 7 / 40 (17.5%): 31628, 46897, 51-12, 55979, 56563, 8942, 9726 | **CONTRACT (defect in code I own)** | LATENT — costs one round; all 7 recovered and passed | **0.000** (all 7 already score 1.0) |
| 2 | **`answer_position` names a sheet absent from the input** — the agent indexes `wb["Sheet2"]` during step-1 inspection and gets `KeyError: «redacted» Sheet2 does not exist.'`; the sheet has to be created | 1 / 40: 402-43 | **KNOWLEDGE (missing idiom)** | LATENT — recovered and passed | **0.000** |
| 3 | Agent's own ad-hoc comparison code raised `KeyError` while enumerating a rule's dict | 1 / 40: 7902 | task-specific slip, no shared root cause | LATENT — recovered and passed | **0.000** |

Total recoverable score on this val split: **0.000**. Nothing in column 1 is failing.

**Environment faults: none.** All 40 tasks ran, produced an output workbook and were scored. The
9 tracebacks are in agent-authored or template-authored Python, not in infrastructure — no
permission error, missing binary, gateway error, timeout or container failure appears anywhere in
the 40 traces.

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)

| File | Edit | Cluster | Why NOT shipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt.md` | *(none)* | — | — |
| `task_template.md` | *(none)* | — | — |

**The two edits I designed, then dropped:**

| Designed edit | Cluster | Which of the THREE TESTS it fails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Replace `task_template.md:97` with a form that tolerates a bare `Cell` (`rng_obj = graded[RNG]; cells = ([rng_obj.coordinate] if hasattr(rng_obj, "coordinate") else [...])`) | 1 | **REAL** — its 7 target tasks all score 1.0, so it recovers 0.000. Also an **already-refuted** edit: prior-run `cand_0005` shipped this *exact* code (diff read in full at `reused_seed_run/run_suite/candidates/cand_0005/task_template.md`) and was rejected at val 0.975. |
| Add a "create the sheet if `answer_position` names one the input lacks" idiom to step 1 | 2 | **REAL** — its one target task scores 1.0. And it is the shape of edit this run's `INSIGHTS.md` records as measured-harmful twice: *"an edit that only adds defensive code advice to an agent already passing has no upside and a real downside"* (prior `cand_0004` −0.050, `cand_0005` −0.025). |

## Verify-the-fix + blast radius (one line per edit)

No edit shipped, so there is nothing to verify. Instead, the **diagnosis** is verified to the same
standard, because that is this iteration's deliverable:

- **Cluster 1 — verified by exact correlation, not inference.** Cross-tabulating "does
  `answer_position` contain a part with no `:`" against "does the trace contain `'Cell' object is
  not iterable`" over all 40 tasks gives a **perfect 7/7 match with 0 false positives and 0 false
  negatives**: the 7 single-cell tasks (`B1`, `I3`, `B6`, `'Calc'!B7`, `C14`, `'Overview'!B5`,
  `J2`) all crash; all 33 multi-cell tasks do not. The tracebacks show the agent copying the
  template's lines *verbatim* — e.g. 51-12 turn 7 raises on `cells = [c.coordinate for row in
  graded[RNG] for c in row]` with `shown = cells if len(cells) <= 24 else cells[:12] +
  cells[-12:]` on the following line, which is `task_template.md:97-98` character for character.
  The defect is therefore in the capability text, is deterministic, and is not the agent's
  mistake.
- **Cluster 1 — blast radius had the fix been shipped: BOUNDED.** The replacement only changes
  behaviour when `graded[RNG]` returns a bare `Cell`, which happens on exactly the 7 single-cell
  tasks; for the 33 multi-cell tasks (12864, 142-12, 227-40, 267-18, 2768, 37378, 37456, 382-10,
  38462, 39046, 395-36, 402-43, 416-15, 43436, 45635, 463-17, 47798, 48527, 48588, 48620, 48921,
  50768, 53383, 53647, 54144, 55049, 560-12, 59196, 59595, 6698, 7902, 80-42, 9569) the `else`
  arm is the original expression and the `cells` list is identical. Bounded blast radius was never
  the reason to drop it — the **REAL** test was.
- **Cluster 2 — verified from the task input.** 402-43's `spreadsheet_content` says
  `TARGET SIZE: answer_position covers 330 cell(s), across 1 sheet(s): Sheet2.` while the preview
  lists only `Sheet Name: Sheet1`, and `answer_position` is `'Sheet2'!A1:AG10`. So the graded sheet
  genuinely does not exist in the input and `wb["Sheet2"]` must raise. `prompt.md:289` already
  states *"The sheet must exist in your output under exactly that name"* but supplies no
  create-if-absent idiom — a real gap. The agent recovered within one round.

## The correction that matters most for a future run

**"Fixing the single-cell crash regresses val" is NOT an established fact, and this run's
handover currently records it as one.** Both `JOURNAL.md` entries list it as refuted hypothesis
(a) — "prior `cand_0005` added exactly that and nothing else, val 1.000 → 0.975, rejected". I
read that gate reason in full:

```
paired Δ̄=-0.0250 <= 0.2·SE=0.0050 (SE=0.0250, n=40, resolvable effect size 2·SE=0.0500)
```

Its measured move is **−0.025, which is below its own resolvable effect size of 2·SE = 0.050**.
By the framework's own `LEDGER.md` convention that move is `unresolved`, and the LEDGER says in
terms: *"it is NOT evidence the edit did anything to that task, in either direction, and must not
be reasoned about as a regression."* And its rejection was **inevitable regardless of its
content**, because its parent was already at val 1.000 — exactly the position I am in now.

So the correct status of cluster 1's fix is **unmeasurable on a saturated split**, not refuted. It
is still the single highest-value known improvement to this artifact (a deterministic crash on
17.5% of tasks), and it should be tested by the first run that has val headroom — not written off.
The same reasoning downgrades prior `cand_0004` (−0.050 = exactly 2·SE, i.e. at the edge of
resolvability) from "proven harmful" to "one task moved, cause unattributed".

I did **not** re-propose either edit here: re-proposing a recorded refutation to re-learn what the
run already knows is precisely the waste the brief warns about, and with acceptance arithmetically
impossible it could not have paid off even if correct.

## What I deliberately did NOT do

- **I did not manufacture a diff to look busy.** With 40/40 passing, every available edit fails the
  REAL test, and `META_INSIGHTS.md` already names this exact trap: *"an iteration that must produce
  a diff will manufacture a speculative one, which is exactly how the prior run lost three
  iterations."* The prior run's three rejections were all additions to an artifact already at
  1.000.
- **I did not re-propose prior `cand_0005`'s single-cell guard or `cand_0004`'s quote-stripping /
  `range_boundaries` advice.** Recorded as refuted in both JOURNAL entries; re-proposal is
  explicitly forbidden and cannot be accepted this iteration anyway.
- **I did not touch `53383`'s malformed-prefix case** (`worksheet2'!C3:C6`, note the unbalanced
  quote). It is real and it passes; defensive prose about it is exactly what prior `cand_0004`
  lost 2 tasks adding.
- **I did not edit any adapter, harness, scorer, benchmark or environment file**, and I ran no
  command that mutates the environment. Every command I ran was a read: `cat`, `grep`, `diff`, and
  read-only `python3 -c` scans over `trajectories/*.json` and the prior run's candidate files.
- **I did not restate any rule the agent already follows.** All 40 traces show the agent executing
  the 4-step procedure, writing literal values, and running step 3; the instruction surface is
  being followed, so emphasis would add length and change nothing.

## Process & features used

- **No subagents.** The brief suggests fanning out one read-only subagent per trajectory group.
  With zero failing tasks there was nothing to diagnose in prose, and the whole signal was
  extractable by two mechanical cross-tabulations over all 40 traces at once (metrics × task;
  `answer_position` shape × traceback presence). A subagent layer would have summarised away the
  one thing I needed verbatim — the exact crashing line, which is what proved the defect lives in
  `task_template.md` and not in the agent. `META_INSIGHTS.md` from iteration 2 reaches the same
  conclusion: use subagents for wide mechanical audits, not for a small evidence set.
- **Method that produced the finding: cluster on the agent's ACTION, not the grader's symptom**
  (carried over from iteration 1's META_INSIGHTS). With no grader symptoms left at all, the
  residual signal was *tracebacks*, and cross-tabulating them against an input property
  (`answer_position` shape) rather than reading traces one by one is what turned 9 scattered
  crashes into one deterministic template defect plus two one-offs.
- **Checked the gate's arithmetic before designing any edit.** Reading `state.json` and the prior
  run's gate reason strings cost two commands and determined the whole iteration. Recommended as a
  standard first move: establish whether the metric can still register an improvement *before*
  spending the iteration producing one.

## What a future iteration should preserve

Everything. All 40 tasks pass under the current `prompt.md` + `task_template.md`. The load-bearing
parts, in order of measured value: the literal-value / no-formula contract and the `data_only=True`
grading explanation (`prompt.md:13-69`); the ordered 4-step procedure with the mandatory step-3
read-back and the *"verifying costs you nothing but a round"* enabling fact
(`task_template.md:40-166`); the normalisation table; the pre-filled-cell rules and the
discriminating-example rule added by `cand_0002` (`prompt.md:170-280`). Every `{placeholder}` in
`task_template.md` is intact and unchanged.
